Why go: Samui's hills, temples and west coast in one day

A jeep safari is the easiest way to see the island's interior without hiring a car or riding a scooter up steep, unsealed roads. This one goes in an open 4x4 with a guide. Morning stops are a jungle viewpoint looking out to Koh Phangan, a standing Buddha temple, and a swim in a mountain pool at a quirky dinosaur-themed park. After a vegan buffet lunch, the afternoon is spent at a cultural centre in Lipa Noi on the quieter west coast, where you can try on traditional Thai costume for photos.

Because the lunch is fully vegan, this is one of the few full-day tours where vegans and vegetarians don't have to settle for a side dish. Entrance fees are included, so you won't need cash at each gate.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: first-time visitors who want an overview of the island, families with children aged 4 and over, and vegans and vegetarians.
  • Choose something else if: you'd rather drive yourself. The ATV and buggy mountain tour covers similar country. If you only want the temples and viewpoints, a car with driver is more flexible; see getting around Koh Samui.
  • Not suitable: during pregnancy, for people with back or spine problems, or for toddlers. The ride is rough in places.

Good to know

  • Temple dress: cover shoulders and knees at the Buddha temple. A sarong in your bag is enough.
  • Weather: open sides mean sun and rain reach you. Pack sunscreen from January to September and a light jacket from October to December.
  • Swimming: the mountain pool is fresh water. Supervise children closely, as there is no lifeguard.
